test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 11 May, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Who among the following was the last Pallava king?
solution:
The correct answer is Aparajitavarman. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aparajitavarman** was the **last Pallava king.**
 
• The **Pallava dynasty** ruled in **Southern India** from the **3rd to the 9th century CE.**
 
• **Simha Vishnu **was the **founder** of the Pallava dynasty.
 
• **Narasimhavarman I** was one of the most powerful kings of the dynasty who is known for his patronage of the** arts and architecture.**
 
• **Mahendra Varma** was another prominent king of the Pallava dynasty who is known for his **military conquests** and the construction of several temples.
 
• **Aparajitavarman** was the** last king** of the dynasty who ruled from** 880 to 897 CE.** 
 
• He was succeeded by the **Chola dynasty**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The **Pallava dynasty **was known for its patronage of the** arts, literature, and architecture.**
 
• The** rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram **and the** Shore Temple in Mamallapuram **are some of the finest examples of Pallava architecture.
 
• **Mahendravarman I **was the** first Pallava king **who established his capital at** Kanchipuram.**
 
 
• He is credited with the construction of the **Kailasanatha temple.**
 
 
 
• **Narasimhavarman I **is known for his **military conquests**, including the defeat of the **Chalukya king Pulakeshin II**, and his patronage of the arts and **architecture.**
 
 
• He is credited with the construction of the **Shore Temple **and the** Five Rathas at Mahabalipuram.**
 
 
 
• **Simhavishnu **was a powerful king who is known for his **military conquests**, including the **annexation of the Chera and Chola** kingdoms.
 
 
• He is credited with the construction of several temples, including the **Vaikuntha Perumal temple** and the **Muktheeswarar temple.**
